arxiv-1905-12534.creator: Ricard Durall 1,2,3 , Franz-Josef Pfreundt 1 and Janis Keuper 1,4 1 Fraunhofer ITWM, Germany 2 IWR, University of Heidelberg, Germany 3 Fraunhofer Center Machine Learning, Germany 4 Institute for Machine Learning and Analytics, Offenburg University, Germany
arxiv-1905-12534.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ricard Durall 1,2,3 , Franz-Josef Pfreundt 1 and Janis Keuper 1,4 1 Fraunhofer ITWM, Germany 2 IWR, University of Heidelberg, Germany 3 Fraunhofer Center Machine Learning, Germany 4 Institute for Machine Learning and Analytics, Offenburg University, Germany. Motivated by recently published methods using frequency decompositions of convolutions (e.g. Octave Convolutions), we propose a novel convolution scheme to stabilize the training and reduce the likelihood of a mode collapse.

arxiv-2104-05527.title: A-FMI: Learning Attributions From Deep Networks via Feature Map Importance
arxiv-2104-05527.creator: An Zhang, Xiang Wang, Chengfang Fang, Jie Shi, Tat-seng Chua, Zehua Chen
arxiv-2104-05527.description: Abstract Gradient-based attribution methods can aid in the understanding of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). However, the redundancy of attribution features and the gradient saturation problem, which weaken the ability to identify significant features and cause an explanation focus shift, are challenges that attribution methods still face.

arxiv-2105-13554.title: Nonlinear Explosive Magnetic Reconnection in a Collisionless System
arxiv-2105-13554.creator: Masahiro Hoshino
arxiv-2105-13554.description: Abstract The debate surrounding fast magnetic energy dissipation by magnetic reconnection has remained a fundamental topic in the plasma universe, not only in the Earth’s magnetosphere but in astrophysical objects such as pulsar magnetospheres and magnetars, for more than half a century.

arxiv-2203-15838.title: Late-time asymptotics for geometric wave equations with inverse-square potentials
arxiv-2203-15838.creator: Dejan Gajic
arxiv-2203-15838.description: Abstract We introduce a new, physical-space-based method for deriving the precise leading-order late-time behaviour of solutions to geometric wave equations on asymptotically flat spacetime backgrounds and apply it to the setting of wave equations with asymptotically inverse-square potentials on Schwarzschild black holes.

arxiv-2205-04333.title: Wavelet-Based Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Out-of-distribution Internet Traffic Prediction
arxiv-2205-04333.creator: Sajal Saha, Anwar Haque, and *Greg Sidebottom
arxiv-2205-04333.description: Abstract Efficient prediction of internet traffic is essential for ensuring proactive management of computer networks. Nowadays, machine learning approaches show promising performance in modeling real-world complex traffic. However, most existing works assumed that model training and evaluation data came from identical distribution.

arxiv-2206-07115.title: “If it Bleeds, it Leads”: A Computational Approach to Covering Crime in Los Angeles Thanks: * Authors contributed equally. Author order is based on last-name alphabetical, descending.
arxiv-2206-07115.creator: Divya Choudhary*, Alexander Spangher*
arxiv-2206-07115.description: Abstract NOTE (2022-06-14): This work was done for a class project in Fall 2019 and is shown, unless noted, without changes. Developing and improving computational approaches to covering news can increase journalistic output and improve the way stories are covered. In this work we approach the problem of covering crime stories in Los Angeles.

arxiv-2207-02931.title: Electrically-driven Photonic Crystal Lasers with Ultra-low Threshold
arxiv-2207-02931.creator: Evangelos Dimopoulos, Aurimas Sakanas, Andrey Marchevsky, Meng Xiong, Yi Yu, Elizaveta Semenova, Jesper Mørk, Kresten Yvind
arxiv-2207-02931.description: Abstract Light sources with ultra-low energy consumption and high performance are required to realize optical interconnects for on-chip communication. Photonic crystal (PhC) nanocavity lasers are one of the most promising candidates to fill this role. In this work, we demonstrate an electrically-driven PhC nanolaser with an ultra-low threshold current of 10.

arxiv-2210-04263.title: Complete set of unitary irreps of Discrete Heisenberg Group H ​ W 2 s HW_{2^{s}} .
arxiv-2210-04263.creator: E. Floratos, I. Tsohantjis
arxiv-2210-04263.description: Abstract Following the method of induced group representations of Wigner-Mackay, the explicit construction of all the unitary irreducible representations of the discrete finite Heisenberg-Weyl group H ​ W 2 s HW_{2^{s}} over the discrete phase space lattice ℤ 2 s ⊗ \mathbb{Z}_{2^{s}}\otimes ℤ 2 s \mathbb{Z}_{2^{s}} is presented. We explicitly determine their characters and their fusion rules.

arxiv-2303-17590.title: Going Beyond Nouns With Vision & Language Models Using Synthetic Data
arxiv-2303-17590.creator: Paola Cascante-Bonilla Khaled Shehada James Seale Smith Sivan Doveh, Donghyun Kim Rameswar Panda Gül Varol Aude Oliva, Vicente Ordonez Rogerio Feris Leonid Karlinsky
arxiv-2303-17590.description: Abstract Large-scale pre-trained Vision & Language (VL) models have shown remarkable performance in many applications, enabling replacing a fixed set of supported classes with zero-shot open vocabulary reasoning over (almost arbitrary) natural language prompts. However, recent works have uncovered a fundamental weakness of these models.

pmc-10554167.title: THU096 When TSH Alone Is Not Enough
pmc-10554167.creator: Sanjana S Awasty, Luma Ghalib
pmc-10554167.description: Disclosure: S.S. Awasty: None. L. Ghalib: None. Background: A Thyrotropinoma or TSHoma is the rarest of all pituitary adenomas approximately 1-2%. TSHomas are often only found due to symptoms from co-secreting tumors with TSHomas or routine laboratory testing. Misinterpretation of laboratory values can cause misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment.

pmc-11397082.title: Composite Mineralized Collagen/Polycaprolactone Scaffold-Loaded Microsphere System with Dual Osteogenesis and Antibacterial Functions
pmc-11397082.creator: Yuzhu He, Qindong Wang, Yuqi Liu, Zijiao Zhang, Zheng Cao, Shuo Wang, Xiaoxia Ying, Guowu Ma, Xiumei Wang, Huiying Liu, Brian G Amsden, Young-Sam Cho
pmc-11397082.description: Biomaterials play an important role in treating bone defects. The functional characteristics of scaffolds, such as their structure, mechanical strength, and antibacterial and osteogenesis activities, effectively promote bone regeneration. In this study, mineralized collagen and polycaprolactone were used to prepare loaded porous scaffolds with bilayer-structured microspheres with dual antibacterial and osteogenesis functions.

pmc-11656576.title: Exploring the supportive care needs of families affected by pancreatic cancer: a mixed-methods study protocol
pmc-11656576.creator: Tara Anderson, Gillian Prue, Lisa Graham-Wisener, Susan McLaughlin, Gary Mitchell
pmc-11656576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPancreatic cancer is an aggressive disease with most cases diagnosed at an advanced stage resulting in low survival rates. Family members often take on a role of supporting patients’ needs. Families tend to be unprepared for this and experience high levels of unmet needs and substantial impacts to their own wellbeing, heightened by the rapid deterioration and short life expectancy associated with pancreatic cancer.AimThe proposed study aims to explore the supportive care needs and associated psychosocial impact of pancreatic cancer on family

pmc-12526458.title: Study on Decarburization Behavior in BOF Steelmaking Based on Multi-Zone Reaction Mechanism
pmc-12526458.creator: Zicheng Xin, Wenhui Lin, Jiangshan Zhang, Qing Liu, Andrea Di Schino
pmc-12526458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In this study, the decarburization behavior in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steelmaking was investigated based on the multi-zone reaction mechanism. The contributions of the main reaction zones to decarburization were clarified, and the effects of key factors—including the effective reaction amount in the main reaction zones, the post combustion ratio (PCR) in auxiliary reaction zones, and the carbon content of scrap steel—on decarburization behavior were quantitatively analyzed.

pmc-12528863.title: A case of a resected mediastinal thymoma with spontaneous regression
pmc-12528863.creator: Takahiko Hazemoto, Ryusei Yamada, Mayu Inomata, Ryo Maeda
pmc-12528863.description: Introduction and importanceWe report a case of a resected thymoma with preoperative spontaneous regression in a 76-year-old woman. Only 13 cases of spontaneous regression of thymomas have been reported in the English literature, including this one.Case presentationDuring a regular checkup, chest radiography revealed an abnormal shadow in the right hilum of an asymptomatic 76-year-old woman.

pmc-12617073.title: The Shapes of Clines and Wavefronts
pmc-12617073.creator: Stuart J E Baird, Nina Daley
pmc-12617073.description: Cline theory has a central place in speciation studies. Cline locations delimit taxon boundaries, cline widths scale with barrier strength, and the shapes of clines (smooth or stepped) suggest whether species barriers are mono‐ or polygenic. How cline shapes vary along chromosomes therefore forms part of the genome's species barrier landscape.

pmc-12638456.title: Looking back to move forward: 50 years of epidemiology of lymphohaematopoietic malignancies for prevention, and healthcare planning in Sardinia, Italy
pmc-12638456.creator: Giorgio Broccia, Pierluigi Cocco, Jonathan Carter, Cansu Ozsin-Ozler, Sara De Matteis
pmc-12638456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In previous reports, we showed the diversity in the epidemiological features of the most prevalent lymphohaematopoietic malignancies (LHM) in Sardinia, Italy. In this paper, we reviewed those findings, aiming to: 1) explore the geographic correlation between the various LHM; 2) estimate the standardised incidence rates up to 2017; 3) compare our estimates with nationwide trends; 4) project such trends up to 2030; and 5) predict the expected LHM cases in the upcoming years by health district to assess the adequacy of the

pmc-13234848.title: Beyond genomes: functional signatures reveal evolutionary patterns across the tree of life
pmc-13234848.creator: Antonio Muñoz-Mérida, Antonio Jesús Muñoz-Pajares, Klara Hlouchova
pmc-13234848.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Protein function evolution provides a powerful lens to uncover biological complexity. Here, we introduce the concept of the pan-functionome—the full set of protein functions encoded by the proteome of individuals belonging to a taxonomic group—and explore its evolutionary implications. By analyzing over 1,000 annotated proteomes across major branches of life, we identify systematic differences in functional composition that reflect deep evolutionary patterns.

pmc-13374573.title: “Trauma to recovery”: the role of participatory arts in facilitating recovery from COVID-19-related trauma in care homes
pmc-13374573.creator: Ceri Wilson, Anna Dadswell, Hilary Bungay
pmc-13374573.description: IntroductionThe Artists’ Residencies in Care Homes (ARCH) programme led by Magic Me involved four arts organisations delivering participatory arts in four UK care homes for older people. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the programme, causing substantial trauma to care home communities. Artists paid greater attention to supporting staff and resident wellbeing and recovery from trauma.

pmc-13440812.title: Dural-based metastasis mimicking meningioma: A rare case report
pmc-13440812.creator: B. Paul Sudhakar John, Hershdeep Singh, Moloti Kichu, Parul Gupta, Pallavi Chaudhary
pmc-13440812.description: Background: The incidence of dural-based metastasis (DBM) is 4% of all patients diagnosed with metastatic cancers. DBM most commonly arises from primary cancers of the lung, breast, and prostate. Most cerebral metastasis lesions are intra axial tumors, whereas a dural base metastasis mimicking meningioma is uncommon.

pmc-13556089.title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder in children and adolescents with Celiac disease: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13556089.creator: Halenur Teke, Aydan Sogut, Hilal Tuter Mavi, Selcuk Teke, Yasin Maruf Ergen, Birce Izgi Akcay, Seda Bozduman Celebi, Mehmet Ayhan Congologlu, Necati Balamtekin
pmc-13556089.description: BackgroundAvoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) may represent a clinically important problem in celiac disease (CD), where lifelong dietary restriction, ongoing gastrointestinal symptoms, and food-related anxiety may promote food avoidance beyond gluten-containing foods and contribute to maladaptive eating patterns. Although adult studies have reported high rates of ARFID symptoms in CD, pediatric data are limited.
